data.narrative:
Monaire is a Seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Nishant Kanapilly and Rahul Subramany that has raised $4.1M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a sector universe of nine private peers (including Helion, Redwood Materials, and Electric Hydrogen) and one public comparable (LNZA), though narrow-stage filtering limits direct peer benchmarking applicability.

Stage-progression methodology provides the primary valuation anchor. Using total raised ($4.1M) as a proxy base and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $10M. This method is applicable given the company's current stage and standard market progression patterns, though it relies on the assumption that capital deployed reflects fair entry valuation.

The peer-median approach was not applied due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the Climate & Energy sector—fewer than three datapoints survived filtering, which would render cross-sector aggregation unreliable. This leaves the analysis dependent on a single method. The triangulated range of $9M–$12M (median $10M) reflects conservative to moderate confidence bounds around the stage-progression result. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the 2.5x multiplier for this specific subsector, the absence of direct peer traction benchmarks, and the limited data on Climate & Energy Seed-stage exits and progressions.
